title: Selected decisions for EC3 weak-disposition batch 5

decisions.source: The static EC3 annotations conflict, but the official issue history subsequently removed #432 ISO approval, marked it duplicate, and closed it completed; #593 received PDF TWG agreement and was closed completed in 2025.
decisions.current_behavior: Repeat-letter output (page 28 is BB) is directly tested.
decisions.verdict: No unresolved current source conflict: retain D03 and repeated-letter behavior. Correct ADR0601 and the source comment because ADR0601 postdates but ignores the2025 resolution. Do not add a duplicate finding or test.

decisions.source: Table 234's corrected /I entry applies beyond MultiSelect and the former array-value trigger was removed. The following /V precedence condition remains when V and I identify different items.
decisions.current_behavior: The already committed B26 public test fails: repeated valid display-name entries are collapsed even though I [0,1] agrees with two selected options. Distinct-label and one-index controls pass.
decisions.verdict: Retain B26 as V-array multiplicity behavior, qualified from #468’s specific mandatory case (same export value, different display names). The fixture has different exports, same labels; /I is optional otherwise but agrees with V. Use the tracked test/result, not the earlier scratch draft.

decisions.source: Table402 replacement removes the embedded-file alternative; each URLs element is a URL file-spec dictionary with FS /URL and PDFDocEncoded F limited to RFC3986. Intent processing remains conditional.
decisions.current_behavior: URL file specs are represented but not dereferenced. Separate tests in output_intents_current show page-level intent is lost to catalog fallback when the referenced/embedded profile is unavailable.
decisions.verdict: No unconditional fetch defect is established. Preserve the separate page-versus-catalog source-priority failure and record remote URL resolution as an explicit capability boundary; do not dismiss the row as producer-only where a consumer elects to honor it.

decisions.topic: Direct assertions, notes and narrowed producer forms
decisions.source: #438 and #494 clarify encoded-name/string bytes; #513 is a layout note; #518 removes only the CMap array alternative, retaining a single-dictionary requirement and compatibility obligations; #522 is an informative /Size note; #549 changes the no-current-path painting operator behavior.
decisions.verdict: Existing byte/name, shape, undefined-painting, and parser evidence is sufficient for the applicable reader claims. No unsupported malformed-input rejection is inferred from producer-constraint changes or informative notes.
